roundShape: Full round: edaaae7e changes runtime files (comment_delivery.go, comment_mention_sender.go, model.go, outbox/mentions.go); round-shape.py was not needed to classify it.

implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's seven round-15 tests at head, with every red test beside them; all pass twice. Then drove the reproduction on the real API: round 14's observation (a failed Retry of a queued attempt, no route) now gives the session one copy.

proof.criterion: Review round 7 finding 1: a Retry that fails while attempt 1 is queued never leaves the mentioned session without the comment.
proof.surface: POST /api/v1/issues/LGA-7/comments and POST /api/v1/comments/{id}/deliveries as a person on the local stack (listener at a 4 s round trip; ses-y advertises steer only; LGA-7 has no route)
proof.command: retryfail.sh h15 30 (30 comments mention ses-y on one lane, a backlog of about 4 minutes; the last is retried in aside, which ses-y does not advertise, so the Retry fails)
proof.observed: The Retry answers 201 with attempt 2 failed. The lane later sends attempt 1 ('sent'), and ses-y stores every comment once, in order, the last one included.
proof.negativeControl: Round 14 ran the same script on its build e4846fb7: attempt 1 was settled 'superseded', and ses-y got no copy of the last comment.

proof.criterion: The same, with the issue routed to the mentioned session; and a Retry in flight, or sent, supersedes attempt 1 with no second copy.
proof.surface: The same API on the local stack
proof.command: retryfailr.sh h15 30 (LGA-7 routed to ses-y); retryk.sh flight2 steer 3 2 (the Retry of c2 is in flight from 16.9 s to about 20.9 s, and the lane reaches c2 at about 19.4 s); retryk.sh flight3 steer 3 3; retry.sh h15-aside aside (a Retry in another mode that is sent)
proof.observed: Routed: comment.created is published after 62 s, attempt 1 is sent, the fallback row is settled unpublished, and there is one copy each. In flight and sent: attempt 1 is superseded, attempt 2 is sent, and ses-y stores each comment once.
proof.negativeControl: retryfail.sh, the no-route failed Retry above, gave no copy on round 14's build.

proof.criterion: No regression in the earlier delivery guarantees after round 15's change and the forward merge of main 96a7e5ea.
proof.surface: The local stack: silent listener, two live processes, SIGKILL during shutdown, and SIGTERM with a successor
proof.command: defer.sh h15 40; stealp.sh 45; crash.sh r15person 1 150; STOP_LISTENER=1 crash.sh r15down 1 170; rolling.sh
proof.observed: Silent listener: comment.created within 65 s (p50 61 s), one copy each. Two processes with a 191 s backlog: 45 comments once, in order, and 29 rows settled unpublished. Kills: one copy per session with the listener up; with it down, one copy from 8 published rows. Rolling update: the old process releases its 27 claims at SIGTERM, and the successor sends all 30 once, with ses-a getting c3 before c2.
proof.negativeControl: The controls from rounds 13 and 14 stand for these paths: the deferral took 188 s on round 12's build, and a two-mode Retry gave two copies there.

notes: Every red test (5) passes twice at head; none was modified this round.

Rolling-update order: after the handoff the successor's sweep resent two of the old process's queued mentions together, so ses-a got c3 before c2. Round 12 saw the same thing. The PR promises order within one live process, so I did not count it as a failure.
CI: on edaaae7e, pr-title was green and changes was queued when I read it; the handoff head 3a86b4ff reported no runs.
Migrations are unchanged since round 14 (0148), so the round-14 seed was reused.
